podcast.title: North American Radio Dominance (2007)
podcast.body: In 2007, Three Days Grace received more radio airplay across all of North America than any other rock band, highlighting their widespread popularity and impact. "In 2007, no rock band received more radio airplay across all of North America than three days grace."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Matt Walst Replaced Adam Gontier in 2013; Band Subsequently Broke Van Halen's Billboard Record
podcast.body: Adam Gontier, who had checked himself into rehab for OxyContin addiction in 2005, suddenly left Three Days Grace on January 13, 2013. His replacement was Matt Walst, brother of bassist Brad Walst and formerly of My Darkest Days. With Walst, Three Days Grace has achieved more number one hits on the Billboard Mainstream Rock Songs chart than any other act in history, including Van Halen. "They have more number one hits on the Billboard mainstream rock songs chart than anyone else."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Commercial Success and Sales
podcast.body: Three Days Grace achieved significant commercial success with three platinum albums in the US and platinum albums in Canada. Their worldwide sales are close to five billion units. "Three platinum albums in the US, platinum albums in Canada, worldwide sales close to five billion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Consistently Successful in 2010s (Active Rock Radio)
podcast.body: This Canadian band was one of the most consistently successful of the 2010s, largely due to active rock radio programming. While they largely disappeared from alternative stations, they became staples of active rock radio. "One of the most consistently successful bands of the decade thanks to active rock radio programming was Canada's three days grace."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Early Gigs and Movie Opening
podcast.body: When Three Days Grace first started, they played as many gigs as possible. At one point, they even opened for a movie at a local theater, showcasing their early ambition. "When three days grace started up, they played as many gigs as they possibly could, and at one point, they even opened for a movie at a local theater."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Escaped New Metal Classification
podcast.body: 3Days Grace was initially categorized under the heading of new metal but eventually escaped that classification, a goal many bands fought hard to achieve. "3Days Grace... Most eventually escaped that classification, something that many fought very hard to do."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Evolution from Ground Swell
podcast.body: The group formed Three Days Grace in 1997, evolving from an earlier band called Ground Swell, which started in 1992 but did not achieve significant success. "The group grew out of another band called Ground Swell, which began in 1992, but didn't go very far."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Juno Nominations
podcast.body: The band has garnered a half-dozen Juno nominations, recognizing their achievements in Canadian music. "And they also have a half dozen junior nominations to their credit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Move to Toronto for Breakthrough
podcast.body: Recognizing the need to expand their reach, the band moved to Toronto. There, they met a producer, created demos, and successfully secured a record deal. "Eventually, though, they knew they had to go big or stay home. So they moved to Toronto where they met a producer, created some demos, and landed a record deal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Norwood, Ontario Origins - Population 4,041
podcast.body: Three Days Grace grew up and formed in Norwood, Ontario, a town with about 4,041 people, located east of Peterborough. Norwood is also known for its annual Thanksgiving fair. "Norwood, Ontario, has about 4,041 people. Find it on a map east of Peterborough. It's famous for a couple of things. First of all, there's the annual Thanksgiving fair every October, and the fact that it's the hometown of three days grace."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Overcoming Small Town Skepticism
podcast.body: Despite their later global success, the band likely faced skepticism in their early days in Norwood, with people questioning their chances of becoming famous rock stars from such a small town. "People must have said, oh, that's so cute. You want to be famous rock stars. But come on. Look around. You haven't got a chance. Yeah."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Record for Mainstream Rock Chart #1 Singles
podcast.body: By the end of the 2010s, Three Days Grace broke Van Halen's 20-year-old record for the most number one singles on the mainstream rock chart, achieving 15 number one singles, largely thanks to support from American active rock radio stations. "And by the end of the decade, they broke Van Halen's 20-year-old record for the most number one singles on the mainstream rock chart with 15. Thanks largely to the support they got from those American active rock radio stations."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Toured with The Trews
podcast.body: Three Days Grace toured with The Trews, who often "piggybacked" on larger tours in the years following their debut album's success. "We would do a, a run with three days grace."

xref.title: Extensive Opening Slots
xref.body: Ho99o9 has opened for a diverse range of prominent bands, including Avenged Sevenfold, Korn, Alice in Chains, Three Days Grace, and Prophets of Rage. "Horror has opened up for a Venge 7-fold, corn, Alice and Chains, three days grace, profits of rage and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Extensive Touring After Debut Album
xref.body: The success of "Not Ready To Go" transformed the band's career, leading to relentless touring with "a couple hundred shows a year" in the first few years. They opened for various bands, including Three Days Grace, Evanescence, and Big Sugar, playing in arenas. "suddenly we were getting our first offers to play in arenas opening for bands. And we were on the road all the time, like couple hundred shows a year, easy for those first couple of years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Notable Clients
xref.body: The studio has attracted a wide array of prominent artists from around the world, including The Offspring, Slayer, The Tragically Hip, Three Days Grace, Metallica, AC/DC, R.E.M., Matthew Good, Nickelback, and Muse (who recorded their 2015 album *Drones* there). "Warehouse studios has been very popular with some big names from all over the world."
